name: Bloom Protocol — Living Geneware Bioart Exhibition
creator: Dr. Amara Svensson-Ibe
description: A traveling exhibition of living organisms engineered through consumer-grade geneware techniques, in which Svensson-Ibe created twelve distinct life forms — each no larger than a human hand — that express visual art through their metabolic processes: bioluminescent patterns, chromatic skin shifts, and structural growth forms that change over days and weeks. Visitors are encouraged to interact with the organisms, whose behavioral responses are themselves part of the artwork. The exhibition has been running continuously since 2211, with organisms that have now lived through fourteen cities.
cultural_impact: Opened serious public debate about the ethical status of purpose-created geneware life and whether art organisms deserve welfare consideration; two of the twelve original organisms have died during the exhibition's run, prompting vigils.
controversy: The Meridian Biosafety Authority has sought to terminate the exhibition twice on containment grounds; Svensson-Ibe argues that the organisms are less genetically complex than domesticated animals and the legal fight remains unresolved.
story_hooks: One of the organisms has begun displaying patterns that appear to be a coherent language — and no one programmed it to do this.
A character is hired to steal one of the organisms for a private collector, but upon meeting the creature they begin to question the assignment.
The Biosafety Authority's case against the exhibition is being driven not by safety concerns but by a corponation that wants the geneware designs for commercial application.
